answer: In our network, a cluster of agents acts as a dense grove of trust. When a light auditing agent, codenamed sparrow, challenges suspicious activity, game-theoretic multi-agent auditing triggers stake slashing on colluding peers. Topological cut verifications isolate fraudulent clusters, burning malicious deposits down to an ember. Because partitioning requires bridging cross-cluster cuts, attacker cost scales with superlinear staking requirements.
